title: Nerve Agent / Organophosphate — Antidote Dosing
keywords: atropine 0.05 mg/kg initial double to secretions
pralidoxime 30 mg/kg load max 2 g infusion 8 mg/kg/h
titrate to drying of secretions not pupils
sources: Goldfrank's Toxicologic Emergencies, 11th ed. — Insecticides; Chemical Weapons
CHEMM (Chemical Hazards Emergency Medical Management), US DHHS — Nerve Agents; chemm.hhs.gov
Eddleston M, et al. Management of acute organophosphorus pesticide poisoning. Lancet. 2008;371(9612):597-607
USAMRICD Medical Management of Chemical Casualties Handbook

changelog.change: Initial entry — weight-based starting doses for atropine, pralidoxime (load + infusion), and midazolam; companion to the nerve-agent-toxicity reference.

purpose: Weight-based STARTING doses for a cholinergic crisis. Atropine is then re-dosed by DOUBLING every 3-5 minutes until secretions dry and ventilation is easy — the endpoint is the airway, not the pupils or heart rate. Adults in severe poisoning typically start at a flat 2-6 mg of atropine regardless of the per-kg figure.

formulas.label: Atropine — next dose if secretions persist (double)
Pralidoxime (2-PAM) — loading dose IV over 15-30 min
Midazolam — IM for seizures / severe-poisoning prophylaxis

interpretation.label: Re-dose atropine by DOUBLING every 3-5 min until secretions dry, wheeze clears, and ventilation is easy. Total requirement is commonly 10-40 mg in the first hours and can reach hundreds; follow with a maintenance infusion at 10-20% of the loading total per hour. Do not titrate to mydriasis or heart rate.

Give pralidoxime as early as possible (before the enzyme ages — often futile for soman/GD). Infuse the load, do not push — rapid administration causes hypertension and, rarely, arrest. Autoinjectors (DuoDote / ATNAA) pair 2.1 mg atropine + 600 mg pralidoxime per dose for field use.

notes: Starting doses only. Adults in severe cholinergic crisis usually get a flat atropine start of 2-6 mg IV rather than the exact per-kg figure. Avoid succinylcholine (metabolized by cholinesterase — prolonged paralysis); use rocuronium. Watch survivors for the intermediate syndrome (24-96 h) and OP-induced delayed neuropathy (1-3 weeks). See the `nerve-agent-toxicity` reference for the full picture; confirm pediatric autoinjector thresholds and infusion rates against a current CHEMM/DoD reference at point of care.
buildNote: Formula engine with min()/max() caps — no conditional logic, so adult flat-dose ranges are stated in prose rather than branched. Companion to `nerve-agent-toxicity`.
